name: Isolated Congenital Alacrima

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Isolated Congenital Alacrima

criteria.description: Documented absence or severe reduction of tear production from birth or early infancy
Exclusion of secondary causes of alacrima such as trauma, infection, or systemic disease
Imaging studies showing normal lacrimal gland anatomy without structural abnormalities
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic conditions associated with alacrima (e.g., Allgrove syndrome)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent tear production from birth, exclusion of secondary causes, and absence of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by lacrimal function tests and exclusion of other causes.

searchTerms: no openings in eyelid tear ducts

laboratory: Schirmer test showing absent or severely reduced tear production
Tear film break-up time markedly decreased
imaging: Normal lacrimal gland anatomy on MRI or ultrasound
genetic: No known pathogenic variants identified in isolated cases; genetic testing to exclude syndromic forms recommended
other: Slit-lamp examination revealing corneal epithelial defects and conjunctival dryness

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of achalasia, adrenal insufficiency, and neurological symptoms
Presence of systemic autoimmune markers (e.g., ANA, SSA/SSB antibodies)
Associated systemic autoimmune diseases like Sjögren syndrome

redFlags: Development of neurological symptoms suggestive of syndromic involvement
Signs of adrenal insufficiency or achalasia
Rapidly progressive corneal ulceration or infection
references: Davis, J. L. et al. (2019). Congenital alacrima: Clinical features and management. Ophthalmology Clinics.
Smith, A. et al. (2021). Differential diagnosis of congenital dry eye disorders. Journal of Pediatric Ophthalmology.
